turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, come on in, have a seat right there. I can hear him from here, buddy. Can I get his full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Jalen Brooks, May 21st,

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: I'm his grandmother, Loretta. I have guardianship.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks Loretta, what's been going on?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: He caught a cold about three days ago, runny nose, and then yesterday the wheezing started and the cough got real bad. He woke up twice last night coughing.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How often has he needed his albuterol?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Every four hours since last night, two puffs each time. Well, no, he's been doing four puffs, the school nurse told him four. Last time was around seven this morning.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And does it help?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: For an hour or two, then he's back to wheezing.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, and the daily inhaler, the Fluticasone, is he still taking that?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Um, honestly, no. He was doing so good over the summer that we kind of starved it. Maybe since June.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That happens a lot, no judgment, any fever.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: No, I've been checking, no fever.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Jalen, does your chest hurt?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: He's shaking his head. He says it just feels tight.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any vomiting after coughing fits?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anybody smoke around him, at home or in the car?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: No, nobody smokes. I've gut -carped myself. I'm on oxygen at night, so believe me, there's no smoking in my house.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good? Has he needed steroids or been in the hospital for his asthma this year?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Not this year. He had pneumonia two winters ago, but that cleared up, and he's never been admitted for asthma.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any allergies to medicines?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: None.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, so his weight today is 30 kilograms. Temperature 99 .1, heart rate 118, he's breathing 28 times a minute, and his oxygen level is 93 % on room air. Let me listen. I hear wheezing all over both lungs when he breathes out, and there's a little pulling in under his ribs. He's still talking in full sentences, which is reassuring. Ears and throat look okay.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Is that bad, the 93? It's a bit low, so I want to give him a breathing treatment right now.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Albuterol with Ipertropium in the nebulizer, and we'll rate check in about 20 minutes.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Okay, go on baby, hold the mask.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Alright, it's been about 20 minutes. Oxygen is up to 97%, breathing rate 22, heart rate 130, which is from the albuterol, that's expected. Just a few scattered wheezes now and no more pulling under the ribs. That's a nice response.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: He looks better, his colour's better.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Greed, so this is an asthma flare, triggered by the cold and made worse because he's been off his controller. First, a steroid by mouth. The dose is 1 mg per kg, he's 30 kg, so prognesilone 30 mg once a day for 5 days. The liquid is 50 mg per 5 ml, so that's 10 ml each morning. I'll give the first dose here.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: 10 ml, 5 days.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Right. Second albuterol, four puffs with the spacer every four hours while he's awake for the next two days, then just as needed.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Third,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: restart the fluticasone, the 44 micrograms, two puffs twice a day, and have him rinse his mouth after. That one he needs every day, even when he feels fine.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Okay, I'll put it next to his toothbrush.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Great idea. I'm updating his asthma action plan, and I'll print one for the nurse at Garfield Elementary. He can go back to school when he's not needing Albuterol more than every four hours.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Okay, can you check his insurance is still the same? The member ID is M, as in Mary 6620418. Got it, that matches.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: If he needs Albuterol more often than every four hours, can't speak in full sentences, his ribs are pulling in, or his lips look blue, go to the emergency room. I want to see him back on Friday to recheck, and we'll do his flu shot then.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Friday, and the number is still 555 -0129

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Perfect hang in there Jalen
